items.q: What happens after every hit of pleasure?
items.a: Neuroadaptation tilts the balance **toward pain**—craving, comedown, **wanting more**.

items.q: Why does a heavy user feel worse over time?
items.a: They dig a **reward-deficit hole** where the drug only **restores baseline**.
As a **30-day experiment**—about the time it takes to start **resetting reward pathways**.

items.q: When do most people start feeling better?
items.a: After **10-14 days** of acute withdrawal; about **80% by weeks 3-4**.

items.q: What are people really addicted to in severe addiction?
items.a: **Control**—a lever that reliably changes how they feel.

items.q: Why is modern life feeding this?
items.a: Endless levers to **track and optimise** everything erode tolerance for **uncertainty**.

items.q: What is codependency in this frame?
items.a: Using **other people's reactions** as your drug to regulate your emotions.

items.q: What's the antidote to addiction to control?
items.a: **Radical surrender**: accept the limits of control and do **the next right thing**.

items.q: What does Lembke do every morning?
items.a: **No screens** until exercise, breakfast and her routine are done.

items.q: What simple practice builds tolerance for imperfection?
items.a: **Do something you're bad at**, offline, without optimising it.
